title: Group-by report
intro: You are building a tiny reporting layer over lists of dicts, like a SQL GROUP BY and JOIN written by hand. Standard library only. Each level extends the previous one.
rules: Rows are plain dicts. Keep the input unchanged: build new dicts and lists instead of editing the originals.

levels.title: Sum a list of dicts by key
levels.prompt: Write `sum_by(rows, key, value)` that returns a dict mapping each distinct `row[key]` to the sum of `row[value]`. Keys appear in the order they first occur.
levels.signature: def sum_by(rows: list[dict], key: str, value: str) -> dict

levels.title: Join two lists of dicts on id
levels.prompt: Write `join(orders, customers)` that returns one dict per order with the keys `order_id`, `name`, `region` and `amount`, taking name and region from the customer whose `id` equals the order's `customer_id`. This is an inner join: orders with no matching customer are dropped. Keep the order of `orders`.
levels.signature: def join(orders: list[dict], customers: list[dict]) -> list[dict]
levels.sampleInput:
customers = [
    {'id': 10, 'name': 'Ana', 'region': 'east'},
    {'id': 11, 'name': 'Ben', 'region': 'west'},
    {'id': 12, 'name': 'Cy', 'region': 'east'},
    {'id': 13, 'name': 'Dee', 'region': 'north'},
    {'id': 14, 'name': 'Eli', 'region': 'east'},
    {'id': 15, 'name': 'Fay', 'region': 'west'},
]
orders = [
    {'id': 1, 'customer_id': 10, 'amount': 120},
    {'id': 2, 'customer_id': 11, 'amount': 80},
    {'id': 3, 'customer_id': 12, 'amount': 45},
    {'id': 4, 'customer_id': 13, 'amount': 200},
    {'id': 5, 'customer_id': 10, 'amount': 30},
    {'id': 6, 'customer_id': 99, 'amount': 500},
    {'id': 7, 'customer_id': 14, 'amount': 150},
    {'id': 8, 'customer_id': 15, 'amount': 80},
    {'id': 9, 'customer_id': 11, 'amount': 10},
    {'id': 10, 'customer_id': 14, 'amount': 20},
]
for row in join(orders, customers):
    print(row)
edgeCases: Order 6 refers to customer 99, who does not exist
Build a dict from customer id to customer first, so each lookup is O(1)

levels.title: Top 3 per group, sorted
levels.prompt: Write `top_customers(orders, customers)` that, using the joined rows, totals the spend of each customer and returns a dict mapping each region to a list of its top 3 customers as `(name, total)` tuples, sorted by total descending then name ascending. Regions appear in alphabetical order. Regions with fewer than 3 customers return what they have.
levels.signature: def top_customers(orders: list[dict], customers: list[dict]) -> dict[str, list[tuple[str, int]]]
edgeCases: A customer with several orders is totalled once (Ana has two)
